newsitem.title: UK: UK's CDC launches Takura venture fund in Zimbabwe.
newsitem.headline: UK's CDC launches Takura venture fund in Zimbabwe.

text.p: The UK's Commonwealth Development Corporation (CDC) has launched a private equity fund to provide capital to medium-sized Zimbabwe companies.

A statement from CDC said Takura Ventures will invest across a broad range of sectors, including manufacturing, tourism, agriculture and agro-processing, mining, transport, financial and other services.
Each investment will be in the range of Z$2.0 million to Z$15 million per company for a shareholding of up to 49 percent.
The fund, which closed on Thursday, has initial capital of Z$100 million ($9.7 million), and a further Z$40 million ($3.9 million) will be committed by the second closing on March 31.

Initial shareholders are CDC (41 percent), Swedfund, the overseas arm of the Swedish government (21 percent) and local institutions. Local institutions include Old Mutual (16 percent), Zimbabwe Development Bank (12 percent), Barclays Bank of Zimbabwe (five percent) and National Merchant Bank (five percent).

The fund will be managed in Harare under a management support agreement with CDC, who have seconded the general manager Rick Phillips. The chairman of the fund is Godfrey Comwe, the former managing director of Cluff Resources.
